thesis: Edgar mints a free Vampire on every Vampire cast and three replacement doublers turn one mint into eight - but v1.1.0 stopped asking those bodies to connect and started asking them to DIE, and v1.1.1 added two more cards that pay on the death: ten cards convert them into cards, counters and life loss at every seat, and the two checker-passed kill routes are a doubled attack drain and a two-card lifegain loop, neither of which needs combat damage to land.

stages.label: THIRTY-EIGHT SOURCES FOR A DECK THAT CASTS FOUR SPELLS A TURN
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-two lands plus five rocks, and one body that turns into mana. The declared ramp component (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Indulgence, Herald's Horn, Patchwork Banner) is drawn in 67.5% of games, mean turn 3.58, and deck-audit still reads the axis UNDER at 8 copies against a 10-12 target while colour-sources sits 4 short in the worst colour. That shortfall has one address: Bloodletter of Aclazotz is the ONLY cost in the 99 with three or more identical coloured pips ({1}{B}{B}{B}) - enumerated over every mana cost in cards.json - and it is half the deck's fastest verified kill. Master of Dark Rites files here rather than with the sacrifice outlets because its output is mana, but deck-facts flags the catch: its {B}{B}{B} is spend-only-on-Vampire-Cleric-Demon SPELLS, and an activated ability is not a spell, so it accelerates toward a commander without paying for what the commander then does. Bloodletter is a Vampire Demon, so it qualifies twice over. One land is also an engine piece: Midgar, City of Mako's Adventure half, Reactor Raid, sacrifices a creature to draw two.

stages.label: CAST A CHEAP VAMPIRE AND A BODY APPEARS - THE ONLY THING THAT HAS TO HAPPEN FIRST
stages.what_it_does: Nothing in this deck happens until a Vampire spell is CAST. Edgar's eminence fires from the command zone - checker-passed twice, in stacks 002 and 010, which read the intervening-'if' again on resolution and confirm the ability functions from the zone it names - so the ignition half the pilot owns is free and undrawable in 100% of games. The half that must be found is the spell: a castable Vampire is drawn in 95.0% of games at mean turn 2.22, the healthiest figure in the brief, and it is the leg every checker-passed kill proof opens on. The six cards beside Edgar are the members whose contribution is dominated by being that spell - four are printed keywords and nothing else, Knight of the Ebon Legion adds a pump activation and Voldaren Epicure an entry ping plus a Blood token - so they can be cast alongside the plan rather than instead of it. Nighthawk Scavenger is the same card at {1}{B}{B} and sits above the declaration's mana-value-2 line. Voldaren Epicure adds one damage to each opponent and a Blood token on the way past. The point of the stage is not that these bodies are good; it is that casting one of them is what turns Edgar on, and everything downstream is priced off that 95.0%.

stages.label: THE BODIES ARE THE RESOURCE, AND THREE CARDS DECIDE HOW MANY THERE ARE
stages.what_it_does: The thing this engine converts is 1/1 Vampire tokens, and the deck holds no card that IS one - so the stage's members are the cards that decide the count. Three replacement doublers stack multiplicatively on the single eminence event: stack 002 records Anointed Procession + Mondrak taking one token to four (1->2->4), and stack 010 records all three taking it to eight (1->2->4->8), order-independent because each doubler gets exactly one opportunity at the event and any modified event replacing it. The declared multiplier component is drawn in 67.9% of games, mean turn 3.60. Five of these seven also make bodies without Edgar - Bloodline Keeper taps for a 2/2 flier, Mavren Fein mints on every nontoken Vampire attack, Charismatic Conqueror taxes opponents' untapped entries, Elspeth's +1 makes a Soldier, and Legion's Landing arrives as a token and flips into a land that makes more. Read the 400-game Forge result before pricing this stage as a win: on a go-wide refactor, combat damage to players fell 29.07 to 18.20 because 1/1 tokens do not connect. Eight tokens is not eight damage. It is eight things to convert.

stages.label: THE THING v1.1.0 WAS BUILT TO FIX
stages.what_it_does: The three games logged on v1.0.0 (001-003) say the same thing: the deck ran out of steam on card draw; the two logged on the current list (004, 005) report the draw holding and the loss moving to the close. This stage is the answer bloodline bought. Ten of the eleven are draw; the declared component is nine cards and reads 83.5% assembled, mean turn 2.62, second only to the castable-Vampire leg among the eleven declared components - and yet deck-audit still reads card-advantage UNDER at 7 copies against a 10 target, because the taxonomy cannot see Bloodtracker, Champion of Dusk, Preacher of the Schism, Castle Locthwain, Minas Tirith or Midgar's Adventure half, among others it names. Five of these turn a body LEAVING THE BATTLEFIELD into cards rather than reading off casts - Crossway Troublemakers (2 life per Vampire death), Liliana (every creature death), Skullclamp (two cards per equipped body), Bloodtracker (a card per counter when it leaves), and High-Society Hunter, whose clause is 'another NONTOKEN creature' and therefore never sees an eminence token. That is the shape the pilot's 2026-09-01 game demonstrated: an opponent's Goblin Sharpshooter pinging the token board fed the draw rather than emptying it. Vampiric Tutor is the eleventh, and it is not card advantage - it is the reason a 4.1% component reads 9.4% assisted and a 7.8% one reads 15.1%.

stages.label: SEVEN OUTLETS, AND THE THREE THAT MAKE THEM PAY
stages.what_it_does: The component bloodline added and v1.1.1 built on. Seven outlets by role sit here (the eighth, Master of Dark Rites, is filed under mana); six are free - no mana, no tap, sacrifice a creature and get something - and that declared free-outlet component is drawn in 72.3% of games, mean turn 3.16. Indulgent Aristocrat's outlet costs {1}, so it is in the stage and not the component. The outlets turn disposable bodies into cards (Skullclamp, Crossway Troublemakers), drain (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant), mana (Ashnod's Altar) and counters - and the three cards beside them make a death pay IN SIZE, the answer to the 400-game finding that 1/1s do not connect. Cordial Vampire puts a counter on EACH Vampire per death. Elenda, the Dusk Rose (in for Immersturm Predator, same four mana) takes a counter for every other creature that dies and has lifelink, so each death makes her next connect gain more for Vito and Sanguine Bond to convert; and fed to an outlet herself she leaves X 1/1 white lifelink Vampire tokens, X her power - created, not cast, so the doublers apply and eminence does not. Blade of the Bloodchief (in for Unbounded Potential) is the same clause on one body: two counters on the equipped Vampire per death, {1} to cast and {1} to equip, best under a lifelinker. Stack 002 is explicit that Cordial Vampire never triggers when nothing dies - the mint alone is not the engine, the mint plus an outlet is - and Elenda and the Blade read the same event. Two bench warnings, not deck findings: nothing declared measures an outlet and a payoff together (the goldfish's sacrifice cap never binds here, sac_cap_hit_rate 0.0), and Forge's evaluator activated Ashnod's Altar 0 times in 59 castings under both AI profiles on another sacrifice deck. A simulated figure here is a floor.

stages.label: EVERY SEAT, EVERY TURN, WITHOUT AN ATTACK CONNECTING
stages.what_it_does: What the converted bodies actually buy. Two death drains bill on every creature that dies - Blood Artist one target player, Cruel Celebrant EACH opponent, a difference of three-to-one in a pod and the reason they are not interchangeable; the pair is drawn in 37.2% of games and is a two-card component, the thinnest declared here apart from the two one-card kill pieces. Two lifegain converters turn the deck's heavy lifelink into life loss: Vito and Sanguine Bond share the same trigger word for word. Five lords and counter-payoffs raise what a body is worth in combat - a lord or anthem is drawn in 80.0% of games, mean turn 3.17 - and five removal spells answer what the drain cannot. deck-audit reads interaction OVER at 11 copies against a 5-6 target and interaction-breadth UNDER at 3 classes, with graveyard and land the classes it detects no answer for - the graveyard answer left with Immersturm Predator; that is an oracle-text heuristic and a floor, not a verdict. The stage's job is that none of it needs combat damage to land, which is exactly what the 400-game run said this deck could not rely on.

stages.label: FIVE CARDS HELD, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE FREE OR NEARLY
stages.what_it_does: Held, not cast. Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver cost nothing 'if you control a commander' - that is Edgar on the battlefield, not in the command zone, and the goldfish has him cast by turn six in 60.3% of games; Boros Charm is two mana for indestructible on EVERY permanent you control and Teferi's Protection phases the whole board out - reading all five, those are the two that reach the enchantment doublers, since Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will name creatures only. Teferi's is also the answer to a sweeper this deck has no other reply to: deck-audit reads sweepers at 0 copies. Akroma's Will is the exception: with a commander it is both modes, which is a kill spell as often as it is insurance. The component is drawn in 68.3% of games, mean turn 3.63, and deck-audit reads protection AT 7 copies against a 5-7 target - it read OVER at 8 until Immersturm Predator left - counting Mondrak and Yahenni, self-protecting bodies filed in other stages here.

stages.label: TWO CHECKER-PASSED ROUTES, AND BOTH REST ON ONE CARD EACH
stages.what_it_does: Route one is combat-adjacent and does not need damage to land. Stack 003: seven attacking Vampires give seven Sanctum Seeker triggers; Bloodletter doubles each opponent's loss independently because it is your turn, so each seat loses 14, and the opponent at 14 is eliminated by state-based actions BEFORE blockers are declared. Your own lifegain is not doubled - Bloodletter replaces only opponents' loss. Route two is the infinite: Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito (stack 004) or Sanguine Bond (stack 006), both checker-passed as deterministic, shortcut-legal, zero-additional-mana table kills. The honest part is the price. Both routes are single points of failure that deck-audit has already priced: Bloodletter is 7.1% of opening sevens and 4.1% assembled (9.4% with the tutor), Conqueror 7.1% and 7.8% assembled (15.1% assisted). The Haunt of Hightower sits here as the combat close - a 4/4 flying lifelink that grows on every card entering an opponent's graveyard - and it is a six-mana body, not a plan. Two one-card lines and a fatty is a ceiling, and stating it is not the same as calling it a defect.

READING (no stack). Sacrifice a token, draw a card: Crossway Troublemakers pays 2 life per Vampire death, Skullclamp two cards per equipped body. This is the loop the pilot's 2026-09-01 game ran when an opponent's pinger fed the draw instead of emptying the board. READING (no stack). The answer to the 400-game finding. Every death puts a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire; the lords add a static +1/+1 each. A 1/1 that does not connect becomes a 3/3 that does, and the deck buys that with deaths rather than with more tokens.

READING (no stack). The single tutor is the whole difference between the unassisted and assisted figures on both one-card routes: Conqueror 7.8% -> 15.1%, Bloodletter 4.1% -> 9.4% (deck-audit).

The doublers are enchantments and a legend, so the creature-only insurance does not cover them: of the five protection cards only Teferi's Protection (phases out all permanents) and Boros Charm (indestructible on every permanent) reach Anointed Procession and Mondrak. Mondrak's own indestructible counter costs two other permanents.

Every death from the seven outlets puts one counter on Elenda and two on whichever Vampire carries the Blade, read off the same 'creature dies' event that pays Cordial Vampire. Elenda has lifelink and the Blade wants a lifelinker under it (Nighthawk Scavenger, Vish Kal, Elenda herself), so each death adds to the next connect's lifegain, and Vito or Sanguine Bond turn that gain into an opponent's loss one for one. Stack 004 seeds its loop with 'you gained 3 life from some source' and does not say where the life came from; this is where it lives.

READING (no stack). The one arrow that runs from conversion back upstream. Feed Elenda to a free outlet at power X and she leaves X 1/1 white lifelink Vampire tokens; they are created, not cast, so Anointed Procession, Mondrak and Elspeth double them the way stack 010 doubles a single token, and eminence does not fire. What X is on the turn she dies, and whether Cordial Vampire's trigger on her death reaches tokens that do not exist yet, is the open question filed for resolve-stack.

map_disagreements.component: A castable Vampire drawn - the eminence trigger every kill proof opens on
map_disagreements.why: The single most scattered component in the brief - 13 cards, 4 cities - and the reason is that it is the only component defined by a COST and a TYPE LINE rather than by an effect. The map groups on what the rest of the card says, so Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant file with the draw engines, Indulgent Aristocrat and Master of Dark Rites with the sacrifice outlets, Charismatic Conqueror and Gifted Aetherborn with the token makers, and Vampire Cutthroat and Knight of the Ebon Legion with the counter payoffs. The leg that 95.0% of games open on has four addresses and no name. My ignition stage is deliberately narrower - the six members whose whole text is keywords, plus Edgar - which is a reading the map cannot express in either direction.

map_disagreements.component: wincon (this model's stage, not a declared component)
map_disagreements.why: The payload half of every checker-passed kill in this deck files in the city the map names for card draw. Bloodletter of Aclazotz, Sanctum Seeker, Bloodthirsty Conqueror and both loop halves (Vito, Sanguine Bond) sit in city-2 alongside Skullclamp, Night's Whisper, Champion of Dusk and Caretaker's Talent; only Edgar himself, who supplies four of stack 003's seven attackers, files elsewhere - in city-4 'Payoffs' since the re-clustering, beside The Haunt of Hightower, the stage's fourth card. The cause is sentence shape: 'whenever a creature dies, draw a card' and 'whenever a creature dies, each opponent loses 1 life' are the same clause with a different payload, and a cluster built from card text cannot separate refuel from kill. That collision is worth stating because it is also the deck's actual reading - the same deaths do both jobs - but a reader looking at the map will see a draw neighbourhood where the deck keeps its win.

map_disagreements.component: A free sacrifice outlet drawn (bloodline's new engine)
map_disagreements.why: Seven of the thirteen scatter rows are fully coherent and this is the largest of them - six cards, one city - yet the name the map gives that city is wrong for what these cards do here. The six free outlets cluster with Indulgent Aristocrat and Master of Dark Rites in a city the fallback names 'Interaction' (it read 'Insurance' before the v1.1.1 re-clustering, when Immersturm Predator's sacrifice-for-indestructible sat in it). In v1.1.1 they are the CONVERSION layer, and the three cards that make them pay - Cordial Vampire, Elenda and Blade of the Bloodchief - file one city away in 'Payoffs'. Agreement on membership, disagreement on job.

map_disagreements.component: A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn
map_disagreements.why: The three doublers that stack 010 proves multiply together on one event have two addresses: Anointed Procession and Elspeth, Storm Slayer in city-0, Mondrak in city-6 ('Insurance') because its loud clause is the indestructible-counter activation. The fodder stage's other token-makers add a third - Legion's Landing, in the stage but not the declared component, sits in city-5 'Ramp' because its back face is a land. A pilot reading the map would not learn that the first three are the same effect printed three times.

open_questions.question: With a free sacrifice outlet (Viscera Seer or Ashnod's Altar), Crossway Troublemakers AND High-Society Hunter on the battlefield, sacrifice N eminence tokens in one turn: how many cards are drawn, at what life cost, and does High-Society Hunter see ANY of them given its 'another nontoken creature' clause? Also: is a 1/1 black Vampire token 'a Vampire you control' for Crossway Troublemakers, and can the 2-life payment be declined per trigger?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the v1.1.0 engine in one board - the loop the pilot's 2026-09-01 game actually ran - and it is the only major stage-to-stage arrow in this model with no passing stack behind it. If High-Society Hunter is blind to tokens, the fuel stage is a card thinner than the declaration reads.

open_questions.question: Stack 002 records eminence tokens entering WITH Vampire Socialite's additional +1/+1 counter (an opponent had lost life earlier that turn); stack 011 records them entering WITHOUT it, because the only life loss that turn came from a trigger that had not yet resolved. What is the practical sequencing rule - does the pilot cast the Vampire before or after the turn's first drain, and does an attack-step Sanctum Seeker trigger resolving beat a post-combat cast?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is a free two-power-per-token swing on the deck's most common turn, it is decided entirely by play order, and the two tracked stacks give opposite answers on boards that differ only in timing.

open_questions.question: Nothing measures whether a body is actually CONVERTED. The declaration prices 'a free sacrifice outlet drawn' at 72.3% and 'a drain that fires when a creature DIES' at 37.2% independently, but not the pair, and Forge cannot help: its evaluator activated Ashnod's Altar 0 times in 59 castings under both AI profiles and cast Viscera Seer 0 times in 500 games (both bench measurements on sacrifice decks, not taken on this list). Can the goldfish measure an outlet AND a death payoff together, and if not, what is the honest statement of what this stage's rate means?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The conversion stage is the whole of what v1.1.0 bought, and right now every figure attached to it measures a card being DRAWN. A stage nobody can measure is a stage the deck page will render as green.

open_questions.question: Both verified kill routes rest on a single card each (Bloodletter of Aclazotz 4.1% assembled, Bloodthirsty Conqueror 7.8%), and the deck holds exactly one tutor. Is a two-one-card-route wincon a correct shape for a bracket-4 aggro-ish list that now wins by attrition, or should the kill be an emergent property of the conversion layer with the two named cards demoted to bonuses?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the next branch buys redundancy (more drain doublers, more tutors) or more conversion throughput, and the 400-game run already refuted the third option, which was more bodies.

open_questions.question: Board: Elenda, the Dusk Rose with three +1/+1 counters (a 4/4), Cordial Vampire, Blade of the Bloodchief equipped to Nighthawk Scavenger, Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Viscera Seer, and two eminence tokens. Sacrifice Elenda to Viscera Seer. (a) Is X read from Elenda's last known power, counters included, so four tokens before doubling? (b) Order the triggers: Cordial Vampire and the Blade both trigger on her death alongside her own - do the tokens she leaves get Cordial's counter if her trigger resolves first, and can the pilot choose that order? (c) Two doublers: 4 -> 8 -> 16 lifelink Vampires? (d) Does the Blade put two counters on the Scavenger for Elenda's death, and none for tokens created later?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the v1.1.1 loop in one board - the reason the branch stated for the swap - and none of its four questions is touched by a passing stack. Every one of them is decided by trigger ordering and last-known information rather than by card text, and the difference between 'Elenda dies into four tokens' and 'sixteen 2/2 lifelinkers' is the difference between a body and a wincon.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add High-Society Hunter to the component (currently 9 cards: Bloodtracker, Caretaker's Talent, Champion of Dusk, Crossway Troublemakers, Liliana Dreadhorde General, Night's Whisper, Preacher of the Schism, Skullclamp, Welcoming Vampire).

The deck holds ten draw engines and the declaration measures nine, which understates the axis the pilot's four logged games identified as the deck's failure and which v1.1.0 was built to fix.

Note the caveat in this deck's own history: an authored declaration is not evidence, so this target should be used to read a rate, never to split games for an engine-lift figure. Elenda and the Blade are the two v1.1.1 additions, both death payoffs, and neither sits in any declared component.

The same re-derivation that added the sacrifice-outlet target DELETED two swarm targets on the grounds that 400 Forge games refuted the go-wide thesis; this label is the last surviving reference to it, and a label is what a reader sees first.

notes.note: Revised for v1.1.1 (branch elenda-v1 merged): Elenda, the Dusk Rose replaced Immersturm Predator and Blade of the Bloodchief replaced Unbounded Potential. Both new cards file under conversion beside Cordial Vampire - they are read off the same 'creature dies' event the seven outlets produce, and they pay it in size on a lifelinker that Vito and Sanguine Bond then convert; Elenda's death-into-doubled-tokens is an arrow back into fodder. Immersturm Predator left the conversion stage, the outlet disagreement and the proposed conversion-pair target; Unbounded Potential left unassigned, which is now empty. Two READING lines and one resolve-stack question were added for the new cards.
